Lesson 10.13 · 10 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Agriculture & allied finance

After this lesson you can:
  • Fit credit to seasons instead of months
  • Use field, land and geo evidence properly
On this page
  1. The product
  2. What a BA watches
  3. Journey contract

1. The product

Credit for cultivation and allied activity (dairy, poultry, fisheries), where the repayment source is a harvest, not a payroll. The journey captures land or tenancy records, crop/activity and season codes, acreage with geo-tagged field evidence, and a seasonal cash-flow plan; weather and price risk references acknowledge what no lender controls.

Schedules are seasonal or irregular — disbursement at sowing, repayment after harvest — and crop insurance is the risk transfer that makes the model work. Priority-sector classification usually applies.

2. What a BA watches

Offline field service is real here: capture happens where connectivity doesn't. Calamity restructure is a designed path, not an exception — weather events trigger recognised relief mechanics with their own classification treatment. Field evidence integrity (geo, time, photos) substitutes for the paper trail urban lending takes for granted.

Knowledge check

1. Why are agri schedules irregular rather than monthly?

  1. Rural banking hours
  2. Repayment capacity arrives with the harvest — the schedule mirrors the crop cycle
  3. Regulation forbids EMIs
  4. Interest is seasonal
Show answer

B. Matching instalments to seasonal cash flow is the whole design; monthly EMIs against harvest income manufacture delinquency.
